resolutions.researcher_notes: SUMED consists of two parallel 42in lines with a stated TOTAL/combined capacity of 2.5 million bpd (Wikipedia: 'Its capacity is 2.5 million barrels per day'; Al Jazeera 2020, citing the designed capacity: 'designed to pump 2.5 million barrels ... every day'; Khaleej Times: 'capacity of 2.5 million barrels of oil a day'). None of these break capacity out per line. The sheet's 'Pipeline 1' value of 1,250,000.00 bpd is exactly half of 2.5M, consistent with two equal lines, but that is an inference from the total, not a value any source states -- per the no-orphan/don't-cite-a-mismatched-value rule, left unresolved rather than citing the total figure as support for the per-line figure.

Wikipedia: the pipeline runs 'from the Ain Sokhna terminal in the Gulf of Suez, the northernmost terminus of the Red Sea'. Khaleej Times (2007): 'The 320-km pipeline, which links Ain Sukhna terminal on the Gulf of Suez to the terminal at Sidi Kerir'. Two independent agreeing sources name Gulf of Suez as the sea/location of the pipeline's origin terminal.

SUMED's own operator site: 'The two 42 inch pipelines extends for 320 kilometers starting from Ain Sukhna to reach Alexandria - Sidi Kerir terminal.' Wikipedia independently: pipeline runs 'from the Ain Sokhna terminal in the Gulf of Suez'. Khaleej Times (checked, not listed to keep the ref count tight) agrees as a third source. Two-to-three independent agreeing sources name Ain Sukhna/Ain Sokhna terminal as the start point.
